name: Creative Chemistry
tagline: Chemistry meets art, design, and unconventional thinking.
seo_title: Creative Chemistry — chemistry meets art and design | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Creative Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: where chemistry meets art, design and creative thinking.

definition.lead: Creative Chemistry explores where chemistry meets art, design and unconventional thinking: pigments, fireworks, perfume, photography, and the creativity behind discovery itself.
definition.body: Every colour on a painter's palette, every firework and every fragrance is applied chemistry. And designing a new molecule is itself a creative act, closer to architecture than to following a recipe.

timeline.title: The first surviving photograph
timeline.text: Nicéphore Niépce captures a view from his window on a coated plate.

timeline.title: The daguerreotype
timeline.text: Louis Daguerre's process is announced to the world.

timeline.title: Mauve
timeline.text: William Perkin's mauveine starts a craze for purple.

timeline.title: Synthetic scent
timeline.text: Fougère Royale, one of the first perfumes built around a synthetic molecule (coumarin), is launched.

timeline.title: Aldehydes in perfume
timeline.text: Chanel No. 5 makes bold use of synthetic aldehydes.
timeline.why: Synthetic molecules became an artistic signature.

timeline.title: Molecular gastronomy
timeline.text: Hervé This and Nicholas Kurti coin the term.
timeline.why: Chemistry as a creative force in cooking.

timeline.title: YInMn blue
timeline.text: Mas Subramanian's team at Oregon State discovers a new blue pigment while studying electronic materials.
timeline.why: The first new inorganic blue in about two centuries.

timeline.title: Ultra-black
timeline.text: Vantablack, made of carbon nanotubes, absorbs almost all visible light.
timeline.why: A material that looks like a hole in space.
